title: Measuring synaptic transmission and plasticity with fEPSP recordings in behaving mice
protocol: Cut 4 cm of stainless-steel wire.
Expose 3 mm from both sides of the wire.
Secure the wire tightly between your fingernails or a hemostat.
Place the wire 3 mm within fine tweezers and apply a small amount of pressure.
Rapidly pull the tweezers to remove the protective sheet from the edge of the wire.
Solder one end of the wire to the head of the screw.
Place the screw on a table such that the shank is pointed upwards.
Solder the tip of the wire to the edge of the head.
Wrap the wire around the screw base and solder them together.
Solder the other end of the ground wire to a connector pin.
Solder both ends of a wire to the remaining two pins of the connector.
Use a magnetic stirrer to twist the wire.
Cut the wire such that there is a 1 mm height difference between the two tips.
File the sharp edges of the cannula tube with a rotary tool.
Measure and log the length of the cannula.
Prepare a filler rod and bend it before placing it within the cannula.
Wrap wire around the head, avoiding the threads.
Solder the wrapped wire at a point other than the first to ensure both drive and threads are clear from tin.
Clean the screw from any remaining soldering flux.
Loop the free end of the wire around the tip of a thin tweezer to make a large enough loop for connector pin insertion.
Pass the connector pin through the wire loop.
Apply soldering flux and solder the wire to the connector pin.
Cut excess length of the pin with a cutter.
Cover the soldered pin with light-curable glue and cure the glue, using as little glue as possible.
Cut 10 cm of stainless-steel wire.
Expose 3 mm from both sides of the wire.
Loop the exposed ends of the wire.
Solder each end of the wire to adjacent pin connectors.
Twist the connector relative to the farthest end of the loop to a thread pitch of approximately 0.5 (i.e., 1 complete turn every two mm).
Cover the pins and soldered wires with light curable glue.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Add 7.5 mM sterile NaOH to achieve a stock concentration of 1.25 mg/ml for leptin.
Bend the electrodes to 90° twice: first at 2 mm and then again at 10 mm from the connector.
Place the mouse in the stereotaxic instrument and remove hair from the scalp.
Cut the scalp of the mouse.
Expose the skull using hydrogen peroxide and perform incisions with a scalpel.
Mark implant coordinates on the exposed skull.
Drill holes in the skull for the implants.
Cover the drilled holes with Gelfoam.
Insert the ground screw into the prepared hole.
Insert the cannula at the marked position.
Cover the cannula and ground screw with Metabond.
Place the recording electrode and stimulating electrode at their final positions.
Cover the electrodes with Metabond once they are localized properly.
Cover all implants, including connectors, with dental acrylic before releasing the manipulators.
Finalize the head construct with dental acrylic.
Insert the electrodes at a 90° angle to the skull surface.
Align the electrodes carefully to the manipulator during the surgical procedure.
Ensure that electrodes are straight and have no bends other than 90°.
Grade the wires of recording electrodes so that one wire is positioned at the target site and another wire is positioned at a distant site inert to the stimulation.
Position the wires at CA1 stratum radiatum and the sensory cortex 1 mm dorsal to CA1 for SC synapse recordings.
Use the ground screw from step 1 as the reference potential for both wires when recording from regions other than the hippocampus.
Generate two fEPSP signals from one implant using a single ground screw in non-hippocampal regions.
Position an inert wire as the reference to produce cleaner signals mainly because noise is manifested similarly on conductors with identical properties in the hippocampus.
Measure resistance with a multimeter between the tip of each wire and the connector pins to ensure conductance is exclusive to appropriate pairs.
Connect a male connector to the female connector for easy access to the connector and wire tips.
Attach rigid metal wires to the multimeter probes.
Cut approximately 7 mm of the cannula tube (HTX-23T-30) with a cutter.
File both ends of the cut cannula tube with the rotary tool cutting wheel.
Polish both ends of the tube with coarse grit sandpaper.
Clean the interior side of the tube with water.
Dry the tube completely with an air duster.
Measure and log in a notebook the length of the cannula.
Prepare the filler rod from tube (HTX-28R-30) as described previously.
Bend the filler rod 2 mm from its edge to form a ∼90° angle.
Anesthetize the mouse with isoflurane vaporized at a rate of 350 mL/min until the animal lies still and has slow respiration.
Place the anesthetized mouse on the stereotaxic instrument.
Set the heating pad temperature to 34°C.
Insert the rectal probe.
Inject i.p. the Ketamine/Xylazine solution.
Gradually reduce the concentration and flow rate of Isoflurane to 1% at 150 mL/min.
Monitor the animal’s anesthesia depth by occasionally testing the toe pinch reflex and observing its respiration rate.
Prepare the mouse for incision of the scalp.
Fixate the head of the mouse to the stereotaxic instrument.
Inject s.c. the Carprofen solution.
Spread eye protecting cream on the animal’s eyes.
Remove all hair from the scalp with scissors and/or hair removal cream.
Clean the surface of the scalp with povidone-iodine.
Wash the scalp with ethanol 70%.
Expose the skull.
Make an incision along the midline of the scalp from the area between the eyes to the back of the head with a scalpel or scissors.
Spread both sides of the scalp with bulldog serrefines.
Remove the aponeurosis and periosteum with a drop of 3% hydrogen peroxide.
Clean the skull with PBS.
Perform horizontal and vertical incisions to the skull with a scalpel without penetrating the skull.
Mark implant coordinates.
Measure the anteroposterior (AP) distance between bregma and lambda.
Log the AP distance for adult mice, which should be 3.7–4.7 mm.
Align the head on all three axes: pitch, yaw, and roll.
Check that bregma and lambda are aligned in the dorsoventral axis for pitch alignment.
Check that bregma and lambda are aligned in the lateromedial axis for yaw alignment.
Verify that the DV height is identical ±2.5 mm lateral to bregma for roll alignment.
Connect a needle to the manipulator.
Mark the desired coordinates for all implants (electrodes, cannula/s, and ground screw) by applying ink to the needle tip.
Prepare craniotomies by holding the drill by hand or with a stereotaxic manipulator.
Slowly lower the drill to the skull surface.
Gradually remove bits of skull by alternately lowering and retreating the drill.
Prevent overheating of the skull during drilling.
Clean the skull with PBS.
Cover craniotomies with Gelfoam soaked in PBS.
Coagulate the brain surface if bleeding occurs.
Maintain the brain tissue wet while mounting electrodes to the stereotaxic instrument.
Protect craniotomies from Metabond applied in step 11.
Insert the ground electrode into the hole using a screwdriver.
Leave a small gap between the screw head and the skull.
Remove dura with fine curved tweezers before step 8.d if surgery is on rats or implants are less rigid.
Implant the cannula to its proper location.
Connect a small needle (e.g., 27 gauge) to the manipulator.
Pass the needle through the cannula until it almost emerges from the other side of the cannula.
Glue the cannula in place with adhesive tape or plasticine.
Insert the cannula into the brain until reaching the proper coordinates.
Validate the length of the cannula before implantation.
Advance the implant very slowly, about 300 μm every 10 seconds.
Secure the cannula and ground screw with Metabond.
Ensure the skull is completely dry before applying Metabond.
Insert the electrodes to the brain.
Connect the electrodes to the electrophysiological setup.
Ensure cables are long enough for free movement of the electrodes.
Mount the recording and stimulating electrodes on manipulators.
Move the electrodes towards their holes and manually adjust alignment.
Position both electrodes perpendicular to the bregma-lambda plane in AP and LM axes.
Align the line between wire tips of the stimulating electrode perpendicularly to the direction of axon travel.
Space out the recording and stimulating electrodes to prevent collision during implantation.
Insert electrodes 200–300 μm into the brain.
Adjust manipulator angle if inserting into midline structures to avoid puncturing sagittal sinus.
Do not bend electrodes to achieve desired angle.
Search for an evoked response by lowering stimulating electrode 0.5 mm above target depth.
Start recording while delivering a medium (0.04–0.1 mA) intensity stimulus at 0.5 Hz.
Lower the recording electrode 0.5 mm above the target depth.
Lower the stimulating electrode in graduations of 0.05 mm until the best signal is achieved.
Lower the recording electrode in graduations of 0.05 mm until the best signal is achieved.
Inspect the delay of the response relative to stimulus onset.
Check for short-term plasticity (STP) facilitation or depression.
Observe the waveform shape of the evoked response.
Measure the amplitude of the evoked response.
Ensure that deviations from designated coordinates do not exceed 500 um.
Deliver a train of five stimuli at various frequencies for fEPSP recordings.
Measure the slope of each response and normalize it to the slope of the first response.
Check stability of the signal by delivering a stimulus every 20 s for 5–10 min.
Take a break for 5–10 min.
If an acute experiment is preferred, continue stimulation for 30 min or until the evoked response amplitude remains constant for at least 5 min.
Continue with the experiment according to the guidelines detailed in the experiment section.
Acute surgeries typically take more than 5 hours and require that the animal be sacrificed at the end of the experiment.
Cover the electrodes and entire skull with Metabond.
Cover the electrodes and entire skull with dental acrylic.
Wait 10–30 min for the acrylic to be completely dry.
Position the connectors at their final position close to the skull.
Hold the connectors in place with a few drops of light curing glue.
Secure all components including the head bar to one another and to the Metabond surface with dental acrylic.
Apply povidone-iodine to the scalp at the edges of the head construct.
Inject i.p. the buprenorphine solution.
Set the Isoflurane concentration to 0%.
Wait for 5–20 minutes until the toe pinch reflex can be elicited.
Weigh the mouse and log its weight in a dedicated notebook.
Reposition the mouse on the heating pad until it is completely awake and moving.
Place the mouse in its home cage.
Perform baseline recordings.
Connect the mouse to the electrophysiological setup.
Place the mouse in the experimental arena (open field, home cage, etc.)
Characterize the I/O curve.
Analyze the I/O curve with the MATLAB analysis package provided in this study.
Select 1-3 stimulus intensities for STP recordings based on the I/O curve.
Use the head fixation apparatus during recordings to minimize movement artifacts and variability in arousal state if applicable.
Accustom animals to the head fixation apparatus several days before starting recording sessions if using it.
Limit the overall number of stimulations per day to avoid long-term plasticity effects.
Fully characterize the I/O curve 2-3 times a week, such as at the beginning of the baseline period, one day before perturbation, and immediately after perturbation.
Include only 3-5 stimulus intensities in daily measurements that are representative of the full I/O curve.
Perform a recording session as in step 19.
Apply a sham or true manipulation using a prepared syringe and drug delivery system.
Position the head fixation apparatus near the stereotaxic instrument and connect the animal.
Direct the syringe towards the cannula opening.
Slowly lower the syringe to a depth equal to the cannula length.
Inject the solution, logging the volume, delivery rate, and time of injection in a notebook.
Wait 10–20 min after the injection before removing the needle.
Raise the needle slowly until it exits the cannula.
Release the animal back to its home cage.
Wait as needed for the drug to produce its expected effect.
Perform another recording session.
Release a small volume (100–500 nL) of drug outside of the brain before each injection with an electrical pump.
Release a small volume (100–500 nL) of drug outside of the brain after each injection with an electrical pump to ensure the needle is not clogged.
